en.title: Airbus A350-1000ULR Breaks Guinness World Record with 14,388-Mile Nonstop Flight
en.summary: The Airbus A350-1000ULR flew 12,503 nautical miles nonstop from Melbourne to Toulouse in 24 hours and 24 minutes, officially breaking the Guinness World Record for the longest flight by a commercial airliner; the type will support Qantas nonstop Sydney-London services from October 2027.
body: The Airbus A350-1000ULR has officially broken the Guinness World Record for the longest flight by a commercial airliner. Operating as AIB35LR, the test aircraft departed Melbourne at 5:27 p.m. local time on July 27 and landed in Toulouse at 9:51 a.m. local time on July 28, covering 12,503 nautical miles (23,155 kilometres) in 24 hours and 24 minutes. Just 13 people were on board, including three Airbus test pilots, two Qantas pilots, engineers and a representative of the International Aeronautical Federation. The routing crossed Sydney, the Pacific, North America and the Atlantic, spanning three continents and two oceans, with those on board witnessing two sunsets and two sunrises.

The mission was part of the flight test campaign for the A350-1000ULR, developed for Qantas Airways under Project Sunrise. Airbus had to operate one sector with a block time of 23 hours, from push-back to chocks-on, to simulate the longest commercial operations the aircraft will fly. Airbus Commercial Aircraft chief executive Lars Wagner said: "Flying 12,503 nautical miles non-stop, we have fully proven the aircraft's capability to fulfill its mission. And the world record was the icing on the cake!" An additional rear centre tank extends the aircraft's range by 1,000 nautical miles, enabling Qantas to operate nonstop flights between Sydney and London and New York for the first time, over distances of almost 10,000 nautical miles with flight times of up to 22 hours.

The new record replaces one held for more than two decades by Boeing's 777-200LR. On November 9, 2005, the blue-and-white 777-200LR demonstrator nicknamed Baby Blue 2 departed Hong Kong and flew east across the Pacific and North America to London, covering 13,423 miles (21,601 kilometres) in 22 hours and 42 minutes. Qantas has ordered 12 A350-1000ULRs, with the first aircraft scheduled for delivery in April 2027 and Sydney-London nonstop services launching in October 2027 as QF1 and QF2. Sydney-New York nonstop flights are expected to follow in mid-2028 with a flight time of about 18 hours; each aircraft will have 238 seats, including 98 premium seats and a dedicated Wellbeing Zone.

image.subject: Airbus A350-1000ULR F-WULR at Melbourne in July 2026

facts.claim: The Airbus A350-1000ULR officially broke the Guinness World Record for the longest flight by distance by a commercial airliner, based on aircraft data independently validated by the International Aeronautical Federation and flightradar24.

Flight AIB35LR departed Melbourne at 17:27 local time (06:27 UTC) on July 27 and landed in Toulouse at 09:51 local time (07:51 UTC) on July 28, covering 12,503 nautical miles (23,155 kilometres) in 24 hours and 24 minutes.

Thirteen people were on board: three Airbus flight test pilots, two Qantas pilots, five Airbus flight test engineers, two Airbus design engineers and a representative of the International Aeronautical Federation.

The mission was part of the A350-1000ULR flight test campaign for Qantas Project Sunrise, including a requirement to operate one sector with a 23-hour block time to simulate the longest commercial operations.

The A350-1000ULR will enable Qantas to operate nonstop Sydney-London and New York flights for the first time, over almost 10,000 nautical miles with flight times of up to 22 hours, made possible mainly by an additional rear centre tank adding 1,000 nautical miles of range.

Qantas has ordered 12 A350-1000ULRs; the first aircraft is scheduled for delivery next April, with entry into service on the Sydney-London route later in the year, and the carrier also has 12 standard A350-1000s on order.

The previous record was set by Boeing's 777-200LR demonstrator N6066Z, nicknamed Baby Blue 2, which flew 13,423 miles (21,601 km) from Hong Kong to London in 22 hours and 42 minutes on November 9-10, 2005.

Qantas expects Sydney-London nonstop services to launch in October 2027 as QF1 and QF2, with Sydney-New York to follow in mid-2028 at about 18 hours; each A350-1000ULR will have 238 seats including 98 premium seats.

zh.title: 空中巴士A350-1000ULR創金氏世界紀錄，墨爾本至土魯斯不中停飛行14,388英里
zh.summary: 空中巴士A350-1000ULR以24小時24分完成墨爾本至土魯斯12,503海里不中停飛行，經國際航空聯合會與Flightradar24獨立驗證，正式打破金氏世界紀錄中最長民航機不中停飛行距離；此機型將支援澳洲航空2027年10月開辦雪梨至倫敦不停站航班。
body: 空中巴士A350-1000ULR已正式打破金氏世界紀錄，成為民航機不中停飛行距離最長的機型。這架以AIB35LR呼號執飛的測試飛機於7月27日當地時間17時27分自墨爾本起飛，28日當地時間9時51分降落土魯斯，全程12,503海里（23,155公里），飛行時間24小時24分；機上僅13人，包括3名空中巴士試飛員、2名澳洲航空機師、工程人員與1名國際航空聯合會代表。航路先後飛越雪梨、太平洋、北美大陸與大西洋，橫跨三大洲與兩大洋，機組在途中經歷兩次日落與兩次日出。

這次任務是A350-1000ULR為澳洲航空「日出計畫」進行的飛測一環，空中巴士須以23小時的關車至開車時間完成一個航段，以模擬未來最長的商業營運。空中巴士民用飛機執行長Lars Wagner表示，飛越12,503海里不中停已充分證明這款飛機足以勝任使命，而世界紀錄只是錦上添花。該機型加裝後中央油箱後航程增加1,000海里，將使澳洲航空首度開辦雪梨至倫敦與紐約的不停站航班，航程近10,000海里、飛行時間最長22小時。

新紀錄取代了波音777-200LR保持逾20年的舊紀錄：2005年11月9日，暱稱Baby Blue 2的777-200LR示範機自香港起飛，經太平洋與北美飛往倫敦，飛行13,423英里（21,601公里），耗時22小時42分。澳洲航空已訂購12架A350-1000ULR，首架預定2027年4月交付，同年10月以QF1與QF2航班開辦雪梨至倫敦不停站服務，雪梨至紐約不停站航班則預定2028年年中開辦，飛行時間約18小時；每架飛機配置238個座位，包括98個高級座位與專屬健康區。
